chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Jameel, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I said, 'A man buys goods from another man, then leaves them with him, saying, "(Keep it) until I come to you with its price.'" He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he brings its price within the period between it and three days, (the sale stands); otherwise, there is no sale for him.'

key_terms.فَلَا بَيْعَ لَهُ: so there is no sale for him

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a sale where the buyer leaves the goods to fetch the payment later?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies the 'khiyar al-shart' (option of stipulation) in deferred payment sales, establishing a three-day window for the buyer to settle the debt while retaining possession of the goods. In Shia jurisprudence, this specific timeframe serves as a default period for validating the transaction, preventing immediate voidance due to temporary delay, while protecting the seller from indefinite uncertainty. The ruling underscores the importance of clear temporal conditions in commercial contracts to ensure fairness and legal certainty.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Hadeed, from Jameel, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>,

‘I said, ‘The man buys the goods from the man, then he leaves it with him saying, ‘(Keep it) until I come to you with its price’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Either he comes up with its price in what is between it and three days, or else, so there is no sale for him’.
en.sarwar: 11. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid from Jamil from Zurarah

who has said the following: “I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who purchases something from a man and leaves it with him saying, ‘I will come back with payment.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘If he comes back with payment within three days the transaction is valid, otherwise, it is not valid.’”
